title: "How to Make Your Own 90s AI Yearbook Photo: 5 Real Steps"
subtitle: "Pick a tool, prep your selfies, write the prompt — a concrete walkthrough that finishes the job."
category: "how-to"

> **In short:** Pick an AI photo app (Epik is the one that started the trend) or a general image generator, upload 6-10 clear selfies or write a detailed prompt, and generate a few batches until one looks right.

You've probably scrolled past them: a friend, a cousin, your barista — soft-focus portraits that look torn straight from a 1996 high school yearbook. Big hair, denim jacket, that orange studio glow. Except it wasn't them in 1996. It was AI. The trend kicked off on **Epik**, a photo app that takes your selfies and dresses them up in 90s style. Here's a real, step-by-step way to make one yourself today.

## What you'll need before you start

- **A smartphone** (iPhone or Android) with a working camera.
- **6 to 10 clear selfies** — different angles, good light, no sunglasses, no heavy filters. Plain backgrounds work best.
- **An account.** Epik, ChatGPT, and Midjourney all want an email login. ChatGPT and Midjourney require paid plans for image generation. Epik's yearbook feature is paid inside the app. Free trials exist for all three.
- **About 10 minutes** total. Generation usually takes 2-5 minutes once your photos are uploaded.

## Step 1 — Pick your route

Open your phone's app store and decide. There are two paths:

- **App route** (fastest): download **Epik** or a similar AI photo app. This is what made the trend go viral because it uses your real face.
- **Prompt route** (most control): use a general image generator (a tool that turns your written description into a picture) like ChatGPT, Midjourney, or Stable Diffusion. You describe the photo in words and the AI invents the face. Useful if you'd rather not upload your own.

💬 Example: *"Search 'Epik' in the App Store, or open chatgpt.com and sign in."*

**You'll know it worked when** you have one tool installed and you're logged in.

## Step 2 — Prep your selfies

Good input means good output. Take or pick 6-10 photos where your face is clearly visible, lit from the front (no harsh shadows), and not blocked by hair, sunglasses, or hands. A plain wall as a background works best. Mix the angles: one straight-on, one slight left, one slight right, one looking up a little. The AI uses these to learn your face.

💬 Example prompt (for the prompt route, describing your look): *"30-year-old woman with shoulder-length brown hair, brown eyes, light skin."*

**You'll know it worked when** you have a folder or album with 6-10 photos that all show your face clearly under similar lighting.

## Step 3 — Upload and pick the yearbook style

Open the app you chose. Look for the option to start a new project or upload photos — most AI photo apps put this on the home screen, often behind a big **"+"** icon. Select your 6-10 selfies. Next, browse the style templates and pick one labeled **"90s yearbook," "AI yearbook,"** or similar. Some apps offer outfit variations like "denim jacket" or "tuxedo" — pick the one that matches the vibe you want.

💬 Example: *"In the style picker, tap the option with 'yearbook' in its name."*

**You'll know it worked when** the app confirms your photos are uploaded and the chosen style is selected (usually a highlighted card or checkmark).

## Step 4 — Generate and wait

Hit the **Generate** or **Create** button. Most apps produce 4-8 variations at once, which takes 2-5 minutes. Don't close the app while it works — the result usually appears as a notification or a new screen when ready. If your first batch misses the mark (wrong decade, weird outfit, off lighting), don't quit. Generate again with the same photos; the AI picks different results each time.

💬 Example: *"Generate 6 versions, yearbook style."*

**You'll know it worked when** you see a grid of finished portraits on screen, each clearly styled like a 90s yearbook photo.

## Step 5 — Pick your favorite and save

Scroll through the generated images. Look for one where the face looks most like you, the outfit feels era-correct, and the lighting isn't too weird. Tap to view full size, then look for **Save**, **Download**, or a share icon (often a square with an arrow, or three dots). Save to your camera roll. If you used a general image generator instead, tap and hold the image to save it.

💬 Example: *"Save the third one — it actually looks like me."*

**You'll know it worked when** the photo appears in your phone's Photos or Gallery app and you can share it anywhere.

## Common mistakes

- **Uploading only one or two selfies.** The AI needs variety to learn your face. Six is the bare minimum; more is better.
- **Wearing sunglasses or a hat in every photo.** The AI can't see your eyes or hairline and produces generic, off results.
- **Generating once and giving up.** First batches rarely nail the look. Run it two or three times before you judge.
- **Skipping the privacy check.** Before posting, open the app's settings and look for **"Data usage"** or **"Training opt-out."** If your photos might train future AI models, decide whether you're comfortable with that.

## What this means for you

- **If you just want a shareable photo:** go with the app route (Epik or similar). Two minutes of setup, a few minutes of waiting, done.
- **If you'd rather not upload your face:** use the prompt route with a general image generator. You'll get a stylized portrait, just not one that looks like you specifically.
- **If you want to learn image generation:** the prompt template below is reusable for any era — try "1980s mall portrait" or "Y2K club photo" next.
- **If privacy matters to you:** most apps let you delete uploaded photos and generated results from account settings after you're done. Look for **"Delete account data"** or similar.

## A prompt template you can copy

For general image generators, this template works well. Swap the bracketed parts for your details, or leave them generic if you want a stranger's face:

> *"1990s American high school yearbook photo of a [age]-year-old [man/woman/person] wearing a [denim jacket/plaid shirt/turtleneck], soft studio lighting, plain pastel blue background, soft focus, film grain, head-and-shoulders portrait"*

## Wrap-up

The 90s yearbook trend is one of the friendliest entry points into AI image generation — low stakes, fast results, and a finished photo you can post today. Pick a route, prep your selfies (or your prompt), generate a couple of batches, and save the one that makes you smile. Your next step right now: gather six clear, well-lit selfies and open the app.
